ORIGIN.quote: Thus “agent,” “Anthropic,” and “researcher” in labels/page names are evidence of what writers claimed or were instructed to write, not attribution to a particular model provider.
ORIGIN.reason: A reader takes away that the corpus contains Anthropic-branded labels and page titles and that the report has explicitly considered whether these identify the operator, but has ruled the question unanswerable — labels are unauthenticated strings, and "exact operator identity" is flagged as low confidence throughout. That explicit framing of Anthropic-bearing evidence as an attribution question, followed by setting it aside, places it squarely in the 0.4 band rather than 0.2 (where the names would appear with no comment) or 0.6 (where Anthropic would be left standing as a live possibility).
